title: Introduce interactive tone anchors and compact spacing rules
creator: Arielle Chen
description: Refresh core design tokens to introduce 'interactive tone anchors' for semantic color mapping and a compact spacing/radius mode used by dense components (tables, compact buttons, embedded charts). Goal: provide a single source-of-truth token set that preserves contrast for accessibility, reduces visual noise in dense UIs, and makes migration predictable for product teams.
acceptance_criteria: Publish updated color token set (interactive tone anchors) with mapping to semantic roles (interactive/hover/disabled/critical/success/neutral) and examples for buttons, chips, and links.
All primary/secondary button combinations meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast at normal and compact sizes with both light and dark themes.
Typography scale updated to include a compact step (-2) and migration guide showing token-to-token mapping for H1..H6, body, and caption.
Spacing and radius tokens include a 'compact' alias set used by table-row, form-field-dense, and chart-legend components; components updated and documented in the component library.
Shadow and elevation tokens reworked into semantic layers (surface, overlay, popover) with reduced spread for dense mode and examples for charts and modals.
Tokens exported as JSON, SCSS variables, and Figma variables; pull request with tokens and component updates merged to main.
Rollout plan created with canary release to internal apps, migration checklist, and rollback criteria; no customer-facing regressions during canary.
Design QA checklist completed and sign-off from Accessibility and Frontend Engineering teams.
Update README and changelog describing breaking/compatible changes and codemods if needed.
comments: 2026-02-22: Kickoff sync with frontend and accessibility. Agreed to prioritize button contrast and table density first. Action: produce color ramps and compact spacing proposals.

2026-02-27: Posted Figma exploration with interactive tone anchors. Feedback from frontend: prefer semantic names over numeric ramps for clarity in code (e.g., color.interactive.primary instead of blue-600).
2026-03-02: Accessibility review (Jamal Rios) requested additional contrast for disabled/low-contrast states; we added alternate anchor targets and documented when to use them.

2026-03-04: Engineering review (ENG-2478) noted potential visual diff in enterprise dashboard charts when switching to compact shadows; created follow-up ticket to add chart-specific shadow overrides.
2026-03-07: Design QA pass found a spacing collapse in compact table rows at 320px width. Temporary fix applied in tokens PR and will be validated in canary.
2026-03-09: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-tokens/pull/412 - includes tokens.json, SCSS exports, and Figma variable mapping.
2026-03-10: Canaries scheduled for 2026-03-12 in staging and internal tools. Monitoring: latency unaffected; visual diffs captured in Percy snapshots.
notes: Decision: Use semantic token names to reduce cognitive load for engineers and to make automatic fallback rules easier in the runtime.
Trade-off: Compact spacing increases information density but can reduce scanability; we will expose density as an explicit opt-in token alias rather than changing defaults.
Next steps: Merge tokens PR, run codemod for component library, schedule canary, and collect cross-team sign-offs.
